description: The Human Resource Development (HRD) Group of COUNCIL OF SCIENTIFIC AND INDUSTRIAL RESEARCH (CSIR), New Delhi, provides opportunities to bright young men and women in the form of direct Senior Research Fellowships (SRFs) for training in methods of research under the expert guidance of faculty members/ scientists working in universities, laboratories and institutes of Government Departments and recognised laboratories of industry in various fields of science and technology. INVITING APPLICATIONS FOR Direct SRF The Fellowships are tenable in all the universities and deemed universities / IITs/ postgraduate colleges/ government research establishments, including CSIR, R&D establishments of recognised public sector, industrial firms and other recognised institutions. Only Indian citizens are eligible for the award. The award is for fixed tenure and does not imply any assurance or guarantee for subsequent employment by CSIR to the beneficiary. CSIR reserves the right to determine the place of work in India best suited to provide necessary facilities in the areas of science and technology in which the awardee is to specialize. Selected Fellows must devote their full time to the approved research programs. Fellows cannot take up any other remunerative jobs/ assignments during their tenure. ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS : M.Sc./ B.E./ B.Tech. or equivalent degree with at least 55% marks and one publication in Science Citation Indexed (SCI) Journal and should have completed at least two years of post-M.Sc./ B.E./ B.Tech. research experience as on the last date of application, as evidenced from fellowship or from date of registration for Ph.D. OR M.Tech./ M.E. or equivalent degree in engineering/ technology with at least 60% marks. OR B.E./ B.Tech. or equivalent degree with at least 60% marks and two years of research experience as on the last date of application. OR M.B.B.S./ BDS or equivalent with at least 60% marks and one-year internship. OR B.Pharm./ B.V.Sc./ B.Sc. (Ag) or equivalent degree with at least 55% marks and one publication in SCI Journal and should have completed at least three years of research experience as on the last date of application, evidenced from fellowship or from date of registration for Ph.D. OR M.Pharm. /M.V.Sc./ M.Sc. (Ag)/ M.Phil. or equivalent degree with at least 55% marks and one publication in SCI Journal and should have at least one year research experience as on the last date of application, evidenced from fellowship or from date of registration for PhD. Documents supporting the research, teaching experience (not below the undergraduate level), and Ph.D. registration should be submitted online. Those who have been awarded Ph.D./ M.D./ M.S./ MDS degrees or have submitted their thesis for the award of Ph.D./ M.D./ M.S./ MDS degrees are not eligible for the position of SRF. EMPLOYED CANDIDATES : These fellowships are held on a full-time basis. Therefore, simultaneous employment elsewhere is not permitted. However, those desirous of pursuing higher studies but employed presently, whether temporary or permanent, may apply with an undertaking that, if selected, they will resign from the job before taking up the fellowship. The application will be rejected if the undertaking is not provided. STIPEND AND TENURE : Rs. 42,000/- per month during the entire tenure of fellowship or date of PhD viva-voce, whichever is earlier. In addition, each SRF will receive a contingent grant of a maximum of Rs. 20,000/-per annum. SRF will be tenable initially for a maximum of two years or depending upon the fellowship tenure already availed. The term is extendable by one year on the basis of an assessment of the progress already made as judged by a three-member assessment committee. Those who have held or are holding equivalent fellowships awarded under various schemes of all India grant-giving agencies such as DST, DBT, ICMR, UGC, ICAR, etc., may apply subject to the condition that the total tenure inclusive of CSIR fellowship shall not exceed three years. Those who have already availed, or would have availed by 17/09/2026, JRF for 5 years or SRF for 3 years from any source need not apply. The combined tenure of JRF and SRF will not exceed five years. SRF will be terminated from the date of PhD viva voce or completion of tenure, whichever is earlier. Those who are already holding equivalent fellowship should specify the reason for applying. The application is likely to be rejected if the reason is not specified. OTHER CONDITIONS / INFORMATION : AGE LIMIT: Senior Research Fellow (SRF) : Maximum 32 years as on the last date of application. Upper age limit is relaxable by five years for SC/ ST/ Physically handicapped and women candidates and three years in case of OBC (non-creamy layer) applicants. SELECTION PROCEDURE FOR DIRECT SRF : Selection will be made through interviews of candidates short-listed based on their academic records, experience, research publications, and assessment of proposed research work by discipline-wise high-level expert committees. The SC/ ST candidates called for interview will be paid single second-class rail/ bus fare to and fro by the shortest route from the station mentioned in the address for correspondence given in the online application form, from (within India) to the place of interview on production of documentary proof as per rule in force. Merely fulfilling the essential qualifications will not entitle a candidate to be called for an interview. CSIR reserves the right to call or not to call a candidate for interview. description: The Indian Institute of Technology Bombay is an internationally acclaimed autonomous public research university and technical institute in Powai, Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. IIT Bombay was founded in 1958. In 1961, the Parliament decreed IITs as Institutes of National Importance. Post : Senior Project Associate Job Reference Number : 50933052 Project title : Smart Diagnostics of Rotating Machinery: A Digital Twin Approach for Industries using Physics-Based Simulation and AI/ML About the project : Rotating machinery plays an important role across industrial sectors such as manufacturing, power, and transportation. However, the presence of compound faults such as bearing inner and outer race/rolling element faults and misalignment makes fault diagnosis challenging under varying speeds, loads, and lubrication. Existing methods like FFT and RMS often fail to detect these faults in real-world, nonstationary conditions. This project proposes the development of a hybrid digital twin framework for the detection of multiple coexisting faults in rotating machinery. A physics-based simulation model will be created to reproduce vibration and acoustic signals for different compound fault cases under variable operating conditions. These simulations will be synchronized with real-time experimental vibration and acoustics data acquired from a Machine Fault Simulator. The advanced signal processing methods will be applied to the experimental data to extract fault-relevant signal components. These features will be classified using a two-stage machine learning pipeline, identifying faulty modes and linking them to simulation reference signatures for the fault characterization and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction purposes. The project will also develop a Graphic User Interface (GUI)-based diagnostic toolkit capable of real-time input, visualization, fault characterization, and prediction of RUL. The proposed system will be made for use in India’s MSME sector. It aligns with national priorities, including Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat, Sangam Digital Twin Initiative, and Industry 4.0, enabling self-reliant and technologically advanced condition monitoring frameworks aligned with the future of smart manufacturing. By combining analytical modelling, experimental validation, advanced signal processing, and intelligent fault classification, the project aims to provide a scalable, explainable, and affordable condition monitoring solution for industrial rotating machinery. description: TagTIC is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral network that brings together leading academic and industrial partners across Europe to understand how infections drive gastrointestinal cancers and how we can turn this knowledge into therapies. description: WHO is the directing and coordinating authority for health within the United Nations system. It is responsible for providing leadership on global health matters, shaping the health research agenda, setting norms and standards, articulating evidence-based policy options, providing technical support to countries and monitoring and assessing health trends. Post : Roster for International Consultants - Public Health Laboratory Assessments Purpose of consultancy The purpose of this consultancy is to provide specialized technical and operational support to strengthen public health laboratory systems in the WHO South-East Asia Region. The consultancy will support the phased implementation of the Public Health Laboratory Recognition Programme by building regional assessment capacity, facilitating laboratory self-assessments and developing laboratory-specific improvement plans. It will also strengthen national capacity for the detection and characterization of priority bacterial and fungal pathogens through assessments of antimicrobial resistance national reference laboratories, implementation of standardized laboratory procedures, and development or revision of national essential diagnostics lists for antimicrobial resistance. The consultancy will contribute to more standardized, quality-assured and sustainable laboratory services capable of supporting disease surveillance, antimicrobial resistance monitoring and public health emergency preparedness and response. Deliverables Support the implementation of the Public Health Laboratory Recognition Programme Activity 1.1 : Planning, organizing and facilitating regional webinars, country orientation sessions and technical consultations to introduce the programme, explain the recognition standards and assessment methodology, guide laboratory self-assessments, and support countries and laboratories in preparing for participation Activity 1.2: Planning and delivering a regional training-of-trainers workshop to establish a cohort of qualified experts capable of supporting laboratory assessments, improvement planning and implementation of the Recognition Programme. Activity 1.3: Planning, coordinating and participating in in-country technical missions to support initial laboratory self-assessments using standardized assessment tools, identify priority gaps, and develop laboratory-specific corrective action and quality-improvement plans. Strengthen national laboratory capacity for the detection and characterization of priority bacterial and fungal pathogens Activity 2.1: Assessing the capacity, functions and operational readiness of antimicrobial resistance national reference laboratories Activity 2.2: Facilitate hands-on mentoring and remote technical support to selected national reference laboratories to address priority gaps identified through assessments and improvement plans. Activity 2.3: Support development of national AMR laboratory network coordination mechanisms, including referral pathways, specimen transport arrangements, reporting flows and communication between reference laboratories and sentinel sites. Activity 2.4: support adaptation of WHO standardized laboratory protocols/SOPs for detection, identification, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, quality assurance, biosafety, and referral of priority bacterial and fungal pathogens, aligned with national laboratory systems. Deliverables 1. Regional orientation and consultation package for the Public Health Laboratory Recognition Programme, including agenda, presentations, participant lists and summary reports. 2. Training-of-trainers workshop report, including training materials, list of trained assessors, participant evaluation results and recommendations for maintaining a regional assessor pool. 3. Completed laboratory self-assessment and on-site assessment reports for selected laboratories, using standardized assessment tools covering diagnostic capacity, AST practices, quality management, biosafety and biosecurity, data management, workforce capacity and laboratory-network functions. 4. Laboratory-specific corrective action and quality-improvement plans, including prioritized gaps, timelines, responsible parties and resource needs. 5. Standardized SOP package for priority bacterial and fungal pathogen detection and characterization, including AST, quality control, biosafety, isolate referral and data reporting procedures. 6. External quality assessment/proficiency testing improvement plan, including participation status, results review and corrective actions for selected laboratories. 7. Draft or revised national essential diagnostics list for AMR, including priority tests, equipment, reagents and consumables needed for sustainable implementation. 8. Final consultancy report, summarizing activities completed, deliverables produced, country-specific progress, key challenges, recommendations and proposed next steps. Experience Essential : Minimum of five years’ relevant experience working in laboratory diagnostics or related work at public health laboratories or clinical laboratories, or research laboratories. Desirable : • Experience in planning and conducting training activities. • Experience in developing country setting in the area of surveillance and response to emerging and/or re-emerging diseases. • Previous relevant international experience in working for WHO in a developing country context. • Previous work experience in Asia is an asset.
